Skip next section Air Force veteran to be Ram Temple's first CEO 09/03/2026 September 3, 2026 Air Force veteran to be Ram Temple's first CEO A trust that runs India's grand Ram Temple in Ayodhya has roped in an Indian Air Force veteran to be the Hindu shrine's first chief executive officer (CEO) in a leadership shake-up following a donation embezzlement row , Indian media reported. Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra, who retired from the Air Force in April 2026, was appointed CEO of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on Wednesday. According to news agency ANI, more than 5,000 applicants were vying for the post. The temple in Uttar Pradesh was inaugurated in 2024 by India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi, fulfilling a key Hindu nationalist pledge. The Ram Temple was inaugurated in 2024 by India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi, fulfilling a key Hindu nationalist pledge [FILE: January 23, 2024] Image: Ritesh Shukla/Getty Images The temple site has been a controversial flashpoint because it was built on grounds where the 16th-century Babri Masjid, or Mosque of Babur, once stood. The mosque was demolished by Hindu mobs in 1992, triggering bloody riots that left nearly 2,000 people dead. Mishra's appointment comes after the Ram Temple became embroiled in controversy in recent months following allegations of theft involving donations and offerings worth millions of rupees. Mishra served as chief of the Indian Air Force's Western Command during the 2025 Indian military strikes, dubbed Operation Sindoor, which New Delhi said targeted "terrorist infrastructure" in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. "I also consider this the blessings of Lord Ram that after 43 years of service to the nation in the Air Force, He has given me the opportunity to serve Shri Ram Mandir (temple) and Shri Ram bhakt (devotees)," Mishra told news agency ANI. Opposition slams move The appointment has also drawn political criticism, particularly in the wake of the donation-related allegations surrounding the temple trust. The opposition Congress party has questioned Mishra's appointment. "Will appointing a new CEO or bringing in new people in the Trust bring back the donations by devotees? Has action been taken against the thieves?" Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Ajay Rai said in an interview with ANI. "Will the retired Air Marshal take action against these thieves and send them to jail? When will the action be taken and the stolen money be brought back?" he added. Congress leader Imran Masood told news agency PTI that the job was for "saints and seers." And if countries decide to do that, then we're going to have to sanction them too," Rubio said. https://p.dw.com/p/5KiU2 Skip next section Foreign Minister S Jaishankar arrives in Poland, next stop Ukraine 09/03/2026 September 3, 2026 Foreign Minister S Jaishankar arrives in Poland, next stop Ukraine India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has reached the Polish capital of Warsaw as he kickstarts an official visit to Poland and Ukraine on Thursday. During the three-day tour, which runs until Saturday, Jaishankar is scheduled to meet Poland's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski and Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha for bilateral consultations, the foreign ministry in New Delhi said in a statement. The ministry added that the visit is focused on "enhancing bilateral relations" and will also provide an opportunity to "exchange views on regional developments and issues of mutual interest." The foreign minister was greeted at the airport in Warsaw on Wednesday by India's ambassador to Poland, Neeta Bhushan. Jaishankar's trip to Poland comes amid speculation about a visit by Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to India. Earlier in August, Poland's top envoy to India said that Tusk's visit, which would be his third to New Delhi, would send a strong signal for cooperation. There is yet to be formal confirmation of Tusk's India tour. The visit also reflects broader efforts by New Delhi to deepen engagement with Central and Eastern European partners. Following the Poland leg of his tour, Jaishankar will head to Ukraine. Jaishankar's Ukraine visit comes after key Modi-Putin meeting The Ukraine leg of Jaishankar's tour comes days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Russian President Vladimir Putin during the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on Monday. During the meeting, Modi urged an end to the war in Ukraine. Ahead of Jaishankar's arrival in Kyiv, Ukraine's First Deputy Head of the Office of the President, Sergiy Kyslytsya, said on Tuesday that he had met India's Ambassador to Ukraine, Anjani Kumar, to discuss Kyiv-New Delhi ties and India's role in efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine . Kyslytsya said he discussed with Kumar Modi's message to Putin in Bishkek, in which the Indian prime minister urged a "move from endless war to end of war" in Ukraine. "We look forward to continued dialogue with India and to translating this shared interest in peace into concrete steps," Kyslytsya added. https://www.businessinsider.com/family-s.text: This past July, my husband and I decided to end our two-week trip to Poland and the Czech Republic with four nights at an all-inclusive resort in the Austrian Alps. I spent weeks researching all-inclusive family resorts in the area and finally chose Almhof Family Resort and Spa for its picturesque setting and large array of activities for families. Ultimately, our four-night stay in a suite cost about 3,900 euros, or about $4,500, for two kids and two adults. It felt like a solid value, especially considering our stay was during a busy season and included meals, activities, and childcare. In the end, our vacation there wasn't quite the break I expected — but I loved the European family resort model, and I would definitely book something like this again. One of the big things that drew me to Almhof Family Resort and Spa was the included childcare. For the all-inclusive price, we received up to 12 hours of childcare per day for our sons (both under 10). That meant we could take our boys to the kids' club while my husband and I spent time on our own in some of the resort's adult-only areas. The kids' club also offered special programming, and every day was different. Our boys got to feed the resort's adorable pet bunnies and take a nature walk with counselors along the nearby hiking path. They did arts and crafts and played games with children from all over the world. The resort's compact design meant that nothing was too far away, so we could give our kids more autonomy than they normally get at home. We allowed them to leave the kids' club when they were ready, and the counselors called to let us know our boys were on their way back to the room. It gave them a sense of control over their own vacation. It also meant that they didn't always want to stay in the kids' club, so my husband and I didn't quite get the break we thought we would, but we still found ways to relax as a family. At this resort, each family is assigned a table that's theirs for breakfast and dinner, so there's no waiting or searching for seats, even when it's busy. The buffet-style breakfast and lunch made it easy to find options we all loved, like Nutella crepes and made-to-order omelets. Dinner was a mix of buffet options for the kids and multicourse plated dinners for adults. The first night, we all ate together and realized it wasn't the best option for our fidgety kids. The children's buffet made it easy to feed our hungry boys quickly, but it also meant they were stuck waiting for us while we ate our three-course meal. The second night, we fed our boys as soon as the buffet opened, then took them to the kids' club so we could return to the dining room and eat our meal alone. It allowed my husband and me to enjoy our dinner without feeling rushed or stressed, and our kids didn't have to sit still. Being able to do this was my favorite part of the childcare program. When our boys weren't at the children's club, they wanted to do one of two things: swim in the indoor/outdoor pool or bounce at the trampoline park. We swam every day, and the pool design was ideal for families of all ages. Multiple toddler pools with slides and water features served the youngest kids, and the main pool featured a large, shallow platform for little swimmers. A large tube slide and a separate room with smaller slides were also available. Outside, the large family hot tub was perfect for a quick warm-up while soaking in the mountain views. The resort had climbing structures and a huge wooden barn that'd been turned into an outdoor play space. Marble runs were available, and the kids were gifted a large wooden marble upon arrival, making for a fun activity that doubled as a souvenir. Outdoor trampolines, slides, swings, and a tricycle race track were also available. After two weeks of nonstop sightseeing, it was nice to let our kids run wild while we watched from the sidelines with a glass of wine in hand. After this, it's easy to see why all-inclusive family resorts seem so popular throughout Europe. Many include kids' clubs and family-centric amenities with adult-only spaces, so there's something for everyone to enjoy. I expected to use the childcare option more than we did, but I don't regret spending our days swimming and bouncing as a family. Childcare was available when we needed it most, at dinner, and though we didn't get as much adult time as we might have liked, that was our choice. The resort's thoughtful features, including family-centric dining and activities, took much of the hassle out of travel. We didn't have to think about where to eat or what to do because everything was available in one place. Our kids never felt like a bother, either, because everyone else's children seemed pretty noisy and fidgety, too. This all-inclusive stay wasn't the break I expected, but enjoying time with my family in a serene setting was everything I needed — and I would do it again.
